attributes.probed_form: NO source edit was made and none should be, which is the point of this record. The premise was measured first, with a census script run from the repo root against src/, config/GUNE5D/symbols.txt and the built object: it counts the distinct `lbl_8034xxxx` symbols enemy.c references inside the pool run, greps every OTHER unit under src/ for the same symbols, and reads our object's .sdata2 size out of objdump -h. All three numbers below are that script's output at 12b0777e5.
attributes.residual: THE PREMISE IS REFUTED ON THREE INDEPENDENT COUNTS, and the third is the one that makes it not merely bigger work but WRONGLY SCOPED work. (1) POPULATION: the order and the predecessor record both say '~19 extern f64 references'. Measured, enemy.c references SEVENTY-FOUR distinct named symbols inside the pool run -- lbl_80346810 through lbl_80346A6C -- and the run therefore extends to 0x80346A6C+, not to the 0x803469B8 the predecessor record names. Our object emits 0x10C bytes of anonymous pool against a target run spanning roughly 0x264, so the under-emission is ~0x158 bytes, not the ~0x9C the record estimates. The figure is understated about four-fold in count and about half in bytes, and both numbers were quoted into the work order as if current. (2) CROSS-TU OWNERSHIP, which no prior record mentions and which is decisive: FIFTEEN of those 74 symbols are also referenced by src/game/game/gamemain.c -- lbl_80346810, 80346820, 80346830, 80346840, 80346848, 80346850, 80346868, 80346870, 803468B0, 803468B8, 803468F0, 80346984, 803469D4, 80346A28, 80346A30 -- and gamemain.c additionally references TWENTY-FOUR symbols in the SAME run beyond enemy.c's span (lbl_80346A70 through lbl_80346AFC). Today those symbols resolve because the dtk split still provides the unclaimed range. The moment enemy.c claims it, the split stops providing them and gamemain.c's references have no definition: the plan as written converts a passing link into an undefined-symbol link failure, or silently re-binds gamemain.c's constants to enemy.c's literals. Closing .sdata2 for enemy.c is therefore a TWO-TU piece of work that must convert gamemain.c in the same change, and gamemain.c is outside this lane's owned_units. A TU's section being contiguous in the link is exactly why this cannot be done one TU at a time. (3) ORDERING AGAINST THIS RUN'S OWN DELIVERABLES: converting 74 constants renumbers this TU's anonymous pool (@N names change), and claim.law.webfrank-reloc-pin-breaks-on-local-symbol-renumber.20260831.v1 says a permutation rule's relocation hashes bind symbol INDICES. game/enemy/enemy now carries THIRTEEN rules, of which three are permutation-bearing (fn_8004646C, and this run's move_logic00 and move_logic22), so the conversion invalidates them and requires a wf_rederive_pin pass over the unit. That is a re-derivation chore rather than a wall and is not by itself a reason to refuse -- it is recorded so the next lane sequences the two correctly, converting the pool FIRST and re-deriving after, rather than the order this run was given. RECOMMENDED NEXT STEP: a joint enemy.c + gamemain.c pool lane, ordered off the per-@N target addresses af_data_base_census already resolves, with the pin re-derivation budgeted into it. Nothing in this record refutes that the blocker is an under-emitted pool -- the predecessor's DIAGNOSIS is confirmed and its cure is under-scoped.
